Title: What to wear to prom
Description: Prom is often the party where everyone dresses up the most. Usually it's black tie or 'formal', but check what the school or committee asks. Go for something you feel great in and can dance in all night. Men: A tuxedo or a dark suit with a bow tie or tie. Renting is a good option if you don't own a tuxedo. Women: A floor-length gown or an elegant cocktail dress. Consider bringing flats for the dance floor.

Title: What to wear to a birthday party
Description: It all depends on the kind of party. A birthday at home is usually casual or smart casual; a party at a restaurant or venue calls for something smarter. If the invitation mentions a theme or dress code, follow it. Men: At home: jeans or chinos with a nice shirt. At a venue or restaurant: add a blazer. Women: At home: jeans or trousers with a nice top, or a simple dress. At a bigger party: a festive dress or jumpsuit.

Title: What to wear to a business dinner
Description: At a business dinner you represent your company, so choose neat and classic. Business casual is often enough, but with clients or senior management at a fine restaurant, a suit is the better choice. When in doubt, dress slightly smarter. Men: A dark suit, or a blazer with trousers and a shirt. A tie in formal industries or upscale restaurants. Women: A trouser suit, skirt suit or smart dress with a blazer. Understated colours and jewellery.

Title: What to wear to a funeral
Description: Dress modestly and respectfully, usually in dark colours. Read the funeral notice carefully: sometimes the family asks for colour or something personal, like the deceased's favourite colour. That request always comes first. Men: A dark suit (black, navy or charcoal) with a plain shirt and tie. No suit? Dark trousers with a shirt and jacket. Women: A dark, simple dress, skirt or trouser suit. Closed shoes and minimal jewellery. In a church: shoulders covered.

Title: What to wear on a cruise
Description: During the day, cruise wear is usually relaxed resort wear. In the evening, many ships have a dress code for the restaurant, with one or more 'formal nights' or 'gala nights'. Check what your cruise line asks beforehand. Men: Daytime: linen trousers or shorts with a polo or airy shirt. Evening: a blazer; on a gala night, a dark suit or tuxedo. Women: Daytime: an airy dress or trousers with a top. Evening: an elegant dress; on a gala night, a cocktail or evening dress.

Title: What to wear on your first day at work
Description: Think about what your colleagues wore during your interview and choose something just as smart, or a touch smarter. After a few days you'll see what's usual. Neat and comfortable is the best start. Men: Usually business casual: chinos or trousers with a shirt, optionally a blazer. In formal workplaces, a suit. Women: Trousers or a skirt with a blouse or fine knit, optionally a blazer. Choose shoes you can walk in all day.

Title: What to wear to a baby shower
Description: A baby shower is usually a relaxed afternoon, often at home or in a café. Smart casual or something cheerful is ideal. Sometimes there's a colour theme, like pink, blue or pastels; the invitation will say so. Men: Chinos or smart jeans with a shirt or polo. A pastel colour suits the mood. Women: An airy dress, or trousers or a skirt with a cheerful top. Pastels and floral prints are popular.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a baby shower, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a concert
Description: For a pop or rock concert, wear something comfortable: you'll be standing and dancing for hours. A classical concert in a concert hall is smarter, especially at a premiere or gala. Also think about a coat that's easy to check in. Men: Pop concert: jeans, a T-shirt and comfortable sneakers. Classical concert: chinos or trousers with a shirt and optionally a blazer. Women: Pop concert: jeans or shorts with a top and sturdy shoes. Classical concert: a smart dress or trousers…
